--- title: "R for data analysis" subtitle: "Beginner course · Master GPE (CERDI / IHEDD)" description: "Six sessions to learn R: import, manipulate, describe, visualise and report development data." --- This course is for **Master GPE** students (development economics). There are **no prerequisites**: we start from zero, install R, write our first lines of code, and finish with a reproducible report. One development question runs through all six sessions, the **common thread** of the course: > **Growth, health and inequality: what does the data say about developing countries?** We start with three countries (United States, China, India), then move to all countries in the world using World Bank data. The last session ends with a figure for a "briefing note to the minister". ### The course in one picture ```{mermaid} flowchart LR S1["S1 R and RStudio"] --> S2["S2 Import"] S2 --> S3["S3 Manipulate"] S3 --> S4["S4 Describe"] S4 --> S5["S5 Visualise"] S5 --> S6["S6 Report"] ``` **Import** data, **manipulate** it, **describe** it, **visualise** it, then **report** it: each session adds one link to the chain. ### Where we are going By Session 5 you will produce charts like this one: **richer countries live longer, but the gain flattens out** (the "Preston curve"). Every point is a country; the area shows its population. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="true" code-summary="Show the code (you will write this in Session 5)"} wdi <- read_csv(here("data", "wdi_panel.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) wdi |> filter(year == 2019, !is.na(gdp_pc_ppp), !is.na(life_exp), !is.na(region)) |> ggplot(aes(x = gdp_pc_ppp, y = life_exp, size = population, colour = region)) + geom_point(alpha = 0.7) + scale_x_log10(labels = label_dollar(scale_cut = cut_short_scale())) + scale_size_area(max_size = 12, guide = "none") + scale_colour_manual(values = pal_regions, labels = label_wrap(25)) + guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 3, override.aes = list(size = 3))) + labs( title = "Richer countries live longer, with diminishing returns", x = "GDP per capita (constant 2021 PPP $, log scale)", y = "Life expectancy at birth (years)", colour = NULL, caption = "Source: World Bank, World Development Indicators (WDI), 2019. Bubble area = population." ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/hero-preston-1.png){width=768} ::: ::: ```{=html}
Session 1

Getting started with R and RStudio

Interface, objects, functions, packages, RStudio projects and paths with here().

 Session 2

Importing and exporting data

CSV, Excel, malformed files; cleaning column names; saving your results.

 Session 3

Data manipulation

dplyr, tidyr, joins: filter, transform, aggregate, merge sources.

 Session 4

Descriptive statistics and regression

Summarising data, correlations, linear regression and its limits.

 Session 5

Visualising with ggplot2 (and maps)

Grammar of graphics, scatter plots, time series, world maps.

 Session 6

Advanced visualisation and Quarto reports

Interactive charts, the final figure and a reproducible Quarto report.

 Workshop

Dataviz workshop (FR)

Slides, in French: building a good chart, from question to message.

 Resources

Going further

Books, documentation, chart galleries and data sources.
``` ## Before the first session ::: {.callout-important} ## To do at home 1. Install **R**: . 2. Install **RStudio Desktop**: (after R). 3. In RStudio: *File > New Project > New Directory* and create a project folder named `r-course`. 4. Download **[data.zip](data.zip)** and unzip it **into the `r-course` folder**, so that `data/` and `R/theme_cours.R` sit next to the `.Rproj` file (`here::here()` relies on this). 5. Install the packages: paste the block below in the RStudio **Console** and run it **once**. It takes a few minutes. ::: ```r install.packages(c("tidyverse", "here", "janitor", "readxl", "writexl", "lubridate", "scales", "WDI", "gt", "fixest", "modelsummary", "ggrepel", "sf", "rnaturalearth", "rnaturalearthdata", "patchwork", "plotly", "crosstalk", "shiny")) ``` Expected folder tree: ``` r-course/ ├── r-course.Rproj ├── data/ │ ├── wdi_panel.csv │ ├── ... │ └── raw/ └── R/ └── theme_cours.R ``` ## How to use this site - Every session follows the same plan: objectives, explanations with code, **exercises**, then "Key takeaways". - Type the code yourself in RStudio rather than copying it: that is how you learn. - **Solutions are collapsed**: try first, then open to compare. - An error is not a failure: read the message, it almost always says what is wrong. ## AI and code AI assistants can explain an error message or an unfamiliar function. They must not replace your learning. **Always run the suggested code and understand every line** before using it: code that runs is not necessarily correct. --- Content licensed [CC BY-NC-ND 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-nd/4.0/), like pierrebeaucoral.github.io.
